channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Dott to comply with ban on shared e-scooters in Brussels drug hotspots
item.description: Dott told customers that scooters entering one of the 19 restricted zones across several Brussels municipalities will automatically stop.

item.title: Students to protest in Brussels against rising tuition fees on Tuesday
item.description: The French-speaking student protest on Tuesday will be backed by the trade unions FGTB, CSC, and Flemish-speaking students.

item.title: €50,000 seized following alleged drug deal in Brussels
item.description: The Brussels-Capital/Ixelles police zone said on Monday that the cash, believed to be linked to drug trafficking, was found during a house search.

item.title: 'Losing hope': Flemish couple delays wedding over Molenbeek birth certificate backlog
item.description: Even intervention by the Brussels Ombudsman failed to break the deadlock after several formal complaints.

item.title: From ancient Egypt to cat karaoke: Belgium’s first living cat museum opens near Brussels
item.description: Just a few kilometres from Brussels is Catland, a unique museum opening its doors to celebrate everything feline.

item.title: Lorry crashes into Brussels church, no one injured
item.description: The exact circumstances of the crash are unclear as of yet.

item.title: MashaaDunya, the festival that celebrates the culture of Brussels diasporas
item.description: Celebrating the richness of the cultural diversity in Brussels, the festival aims to create space for artists whose cultures are not at the centre of “traditional cultural circuits."

item.title: Trapped in the English bubble: Living in Belgium for years without French or Dutch
item.description: What begins as a convenient solution, can slowly turn into years of living in the English-speaking bubble.

item.title: About 100 people protest against violence against children in Brussels
item.description: A new survey suggests more than one million people in Belgium have experienced incest, with 40% of victims never disclosing the abuse to relatives.

item.title: Media Literacy Week to encourage diversity online
item.description: Activities have been tailored to different age groups and will examine where content comes from, how formats work, how representations are shaped and how images can be decoded.

item.title: Palestinian surgeon sues Belgium to secure evacuation of his visa-holding family
item.description: A Palestinian doctor with an aggressive cancer has asked a Brussels court to help bring his family out of Gaza, where they are trapped despite holding visas.

item.title: Housing right groups seek to block sale of two Brussels public buildings
item.description: The Capital Region Housing Company argued that the sale had been imposed on it by the Brussels-Capital Region.

item.title: 'Choose your budget!' shout ULB students rallying on the Solbosch campus
item.description: The organisers said the action was designed to present students with what they described as two opposing visions for society.

item.title: What to do in Brussels this weekend: 13 - 15 November
item.description: Whether you want to brave the cold for a walking tour or are looking for cosy indoor activities, here are The Brussels Times top picks for this weekend.

item.title: US expresses interest in buying Brussels Minister-President’s €45 million official residence
item.description: The US has expressed interest in purchasing the official residence of Brussels Minister-President Boris Dilliès (MR). The Brussels government plans to sell the building to tackle the region’s budget deficit.

item.title: Deadly shooting near EU Parliament linked to Brussels police officer Nordine's killing
item.description: The men suspected of shooting dead Brussels police officer Nordine El Talbi in Jette in October had allegedly killed a man near the EU Parliament that same evening.

item.title: Man carrying two plastic weapons arrested at Brussels Airport
item.description: A man was arrested at Brussels Airport after entering the departure hall with two plastic weapons.

item.title: Belgium unveils 29 measures to tackle online fraud
item.description: The Belgian Federal Government has announced a new action plan to combat online fraud, introducing 29 measures aimed at preventing phishing.

item.title: Student rooms in Brussels now cost an average €705 a month to rent
item.description: Across Belgium's 10 largest cities, the average rent price is now €600 for the current 2026–2027 academic year; this has increased by €10 in the last year.

item.title: Person armed with weapon arrested in Molenbeek
item.description: The individual was seen on Rue Delaunoy holding a weapon and subsequently entered a property on Chaussée de Gand, according to the police.
